prerequisites: Calculation skills and operation with simple geometric and algebraic notions
Abilities to use logical thinking and problem solving

learning_outcomes.text: Explains the fundamental notions of Newtonian Mechanics.
Knows, defines and explains notions regarding: the theory of sliding vectors, centers of mass, statics of rigid bodies and statics of mechanical systems.
Uses vector calculus to interpret the action of vector systems on macroscopic bodies.
Analyzes the effect of sliding vector systems on macroscopic bodies.
Evaluates and describes the type of stress/load to which the macroscopic body is subjected.
Determines the position of the center of mass for macroscopic bodies that may or may not have an axis of symmetry.
Identifies and understands the phenomena and principles specific to the statics of mechanical systems.
Applies equilibrium conditions to systems of rigid solid bodies.
Efficiently uses the physical and mathematical models available in the analysis of relative rest.
Synthesizes relevant aspects in the context of learning.
Solves problems associated with Mechanics and interprets the results.
Critically evaluates the phenomena and principles specific to Classical Mechanics.
Respects the principles, norms, and values of the professional code of ethics by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in problem-solving and decision-making.
Selects and analyzes bibliographic sources specific to the field.
Applies effective communication and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents oneself in their field of activity by adequately using effective lifelong learning methods and techniques.
Develops professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Object of mechanics. Brief history. Divisions of mechanics. Models used in mechanics. Principles and fundamental notions in classical mechanics.
Notions from the theory of free vectors.

Systems of forces. The sliding vector nature of the force acting on a rigid body. Polar moment of a sliding vector. Axial moment. Equivalence operations. Systems of vectors: resultant vector, resultant moment. Invariants. Wrench.

Central axis of a system of sliding vectors. Equivalence of systems of sliding vectors. Reduction of systems of sliding vectors. Particular force systems. Center of parallel forces. Calculation example.
Geometry of masses. Center of mass of a rigid body. Pappus-Guldinus theorems.
Constraints imposed on a mechanical system. Constraint wrench.

Statics of a rigid body. Equilibrium conditions for a system of forces acting on a free rigid body. Rigid body subjected to frictionless constraints (simple support, articulation/hinge, fixed support/cantilever, cable or rigid rod). Calculation example.

Scalar quantities. Vector quantities. Examples. Versor. Classification of vectors. Null vector. Operations with vectors. Sum of two coplanar vectors: parallelogram rule, triangle rule; Polygon rule; Sum of three non-coplanar vectors; Decomposition of a vector along two coplanar directions.

Operations with vectors. Decomposition of a vector along three concurrent non-coplanar directions. Projection of a vector onto an axis. Fixed orthonormal basis. Analytical expression of a vector. Multiplication of a vector by a scalar. Scalar product of two vectors. Vector product of two vectors. Double vector product of three vectors. Mixed product of three vectors.
Orthogonality condition. Collinearity condition. Coplanarity condition. Resultant. Polar moment. Resultant moment. Wrench. Invariants. Reduction cases. Central axis. Minimum wrench.
Calculation of the polar moment for coplanar vectors (lever arm method). Particular case: reduction of systems of coplanar vectors.
Determination of the center of mass for homogeneous planar plates without an axis of symmetry.
Constraints with or without friction. Distributed loads. Equilibrium conditions for a rigid solid body.
teaching_methods: Discovery learning models facilitated by direct or indirect exploration of reality

assessment_methods.method: Systematic observation of students (individual/team assignments and report)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of the minimal learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for each assessed component.
